subject.title: [Feature]: Add a standard AISP/AISOP proposal contract for Skill Workshop

question: Should OpenClaw core standardize a machine-readable Skill Workshop lifecycle contract, and should that contract be OpenClaw-native, AISP/AISOP reference-only, or published outside core through ClawHub?
rationale: This choice determines product and security authority for generated skill writes; automation cannot safely decide whether a new contract is documentation, tests, validator input, runtime governance, or external package surface.

options.title: Core OpenClaw Contract Fixture
options.body: Keep this issue open and define a core-owned contract or generated fixture that is validated by tests against the existing Skill Workshop service without adding an AISP runtime dependency.

options.title: AISP Reference Package
options.body: Keep this issue open but scope it to a reference-only AISP/AISOP package with explicit non-authoritative status unless later adopted by maintainers.

options.title: Move Package To ClawHub
options.body: Close or narrow the core issue if maintainers decide the AISP package is only an optional external package and core should keep docs/tests as the authority.

recommendation.title: Core OpenClaw Contract Fixture
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and define a core-owned contract or generated fixture that is validated by tests against the existing Skill Workshop service without adding an AISP runtime dependency.

likelyOwner.reason: The available issue-history provenance points to this handle as the original Skill Workshop feature owner for proposal storage, service behavior, and lifecycle policy.
